claims.text: The studied material is a solidified, Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
The dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn is governed by thermally activated dislocation glide.
The governing dislocation-glide mechanism is sensitive to temperature.
The governing dislocation-glide mechanism is sensitive to strain rate.
Dislocation density and mobility mediate the dynamic response.
Interactions between dislocations and solute atoms influence thermally activated dislocation glide.
The proposed study varies temperature from -196°C to 500°C and strain rate from 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
Testing is conducted under uniaxial tensile loading with temperature and strain rate held constant within each test.
The reference condition is 20°C at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
At strain rates above 10^2 s^-1 and temperatures below 0°C, yield strength will increase by 20% relative to the baseline.
At strain rates above 10^2 s^-1 and temperatures below 0°C, ductility will decrease by 30% relative to the baseline.
The exact relationship among dislocation density, dislocation mobility, and dynamic behavior in FeNiCrMn is not well understood.
The role of solute atoms in controlling dislocation glide in FeNiCrMn remains unclear.
The hypothesis is falsified if yield strength and ductility do not vary by more than 10% with temperature and strain rate.
